subject: Comparing CFA Factor Scores without missing data to Factor Scores with missing data for an entire variable

messages.author: cd016d159ac3dc3c
messages.subject: Comparing CFA Factor Scores without missing data to Factor Scores with missing data for an entire variable
parts:
Hi, 

I have several cognitive tests that I am loading onto 1 factor (general factor for intelligence, g factor). Only a subset of participants completed all cognitive tests. Other completed different combinations of cognitive tests (e.g. some did test all but test x1, some did all tests but test x4 etc.). 

My goal is to know what combination of cognitive tests (manifest/observed variables) must be completed to generate factor scores that are similar to those that we would have been obtained had the participants completed all cognitive tests. 

To do this, from my subset of participants that do not have missing data, I remove all data points from a cognitive test 1 (let's take x1), to see if the factor scores I obtain when data for x1 is missing are similar to the factor scores I obtain when data for x1 is not missing. If the correlation between factor scores is <0.8, I will not compute a factor score for participants that have missing data for x1 using the CFA model performed on individuals without missing data because their factor scores will be unreliable (will not represent their factor scor had they completed test x1). 

See code for steps described below. 

1. I perform my CFA on the participants without missing data. 
2. I extract the loadings and intercepts and apply them to another CFA: The fixed CFA Model. 
2. Even though I fix the variance of x1 to 1.128, I am unable to run the model. I get this error: Error in lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, cluster = cluster, : lavaan ERROR: some variables have no values (only missings) or no variance

Question: Why am I unable to run the CFA model even though I fix the variance to 1.128 ? Am I forgetting to specify a parameter to be able to do this?
  
#Data 
HolzingerSwineford1939

# 1. CFA on participants who completed all cognitive tests 
G_factor_model <- ' G  =~ NA*x1 + x4 + x5 + x6 + x9 
G ~~ 1*G
'
fit <- cfa(G_factor_model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, meanstructure=TRUE)
parameterestimates(fit) 

FactorScores <- lavPredict(fit, method = "ml")

# 2. CFA on participants who completed all cognitive tests except x1 

HolzingerSwineford1939_no_x1 <- setDT(as.data.frame(HolzingerSwineford1939[, -7]))
HolzingerSwineford1939_no_x1$x1 <- NA #blank column 

G_factor_model_fixed <- ' G  =~ 0.480*x1 + 0.990*x4 + 1.102*x5 + 0.913*x6 + 0.276*x9 
# fix variance 
G ~~ 1*G
x1 ~~  1.128*x1 
# fix intercepts
x1 ~ 4.936 * 1 
x4 ~ 3.061 * 1 
x5 ~ 4.341* 1 
x6 ~ 2.186 * 1 
x9 ~ 5.374 * 1 
'
fit_fixed <- cfa(G_factor_model_fixed, data=HolzingerSwineford1939_no_x1, meanstructure=TRUE, missing = "ml")
Error in lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, cluster = cluster,  : 
  lavaan ERROR: some variables have no values (only missings) or no variance
parameterestimates(fit_fixed) 

FactorScores_fixed <- lavPredict(fit_fixed, method = "ml")

# Compare factor scores 
cor(FactorScores, FactorScores_fixed)

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Comparing CFA Factor Scores without missing data to Factor Scores with missing data for an entire variable
parts: Please help me understand how to manually set the variance for my variable with missing data

The software algorithm is trying to find parameters that minimize the discrepancy between the observed and model-implied covariance matrices. If you fix all parameters, I can see why you would intuit that the software should not have to estimate anything.  But software cannot even get off the ground if the criterion (observed covariance matrix) cannot be calculated because all values are missing on x1.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
